This site mentions the dates of some of the photos. However, that much ice doesn't just vanish on an annual cycle; glaciers aren't here in winter and gone in summer: these photographs really do show a long-term trend. (The article does cite some data too.)

I do think it's clear though that, no matter how bad global warming may be, global cooling may've sucked even worse.

What you can't see is the stress to the ecosystem as other species move north, you can't see the acidification of the water as CO2 levels rise, you can't see the loss of biodiversity as a unique habitat becomes like places further south.

I do think it's clear though that, no matter how bad global warming may be, global cooling may've sucked even worse.

Not from where we were - right near the peak of an interglacial.

The climate has been swinging between glaciations and interglacials for several million years. A cooling would have taken the climate to a state that almost all existent species have coped with. Warming is the cause of many extinctions and collapse of ecosystems.

Similarly, with respect to infrastructure, there is more under threat from the sea than from glaciers, because cities tend to get built on the edge of the ocean, but not on the edge of glaciers.
